pages.title: Proofreading

concepts.label: Proofreading
concepts.detail: A mismatch causes a kinetic pause; 3'→5' exonuclease removes it, then polymerization resumes. Proofreading is not reversal of polymerization and does not involve PPi.
concepts.rationale: Explicitly defined mechanism, comparison, or functional relationship in the lecture.

concepts.label: Proofreading figure sequence
concepts.detail: Rare C* pairs with A and is incorporated, reverts to C, creates a mispaired 3'-OH, is transferred to the exonuclease site and removed before synthesis resumes.
concepts.rationale: Supporting numerical, experimental, illustrative or unresolved detail retained for complete source coverage; no exam likelihood inferred.

concepts.label: Scope of proofreading claim
concepts.detail: Page 14 labels proofreading intrinsic to all polymerases; page 26 explicitly gives pol alpha without proofreading, so the universal claim is unresolved.
concepts.rationale: Supporting numerical, experimental, illustrative or unresolved detail retained for complete source coverage; no exam likelihood inferred.

pages.visualNotes:
DNA polymerase I has separately labeled polymerase and 3' -> 5' proofreading exonuclease active sites. The full figure sequence:

1. A rare tautomeric form of cytosine (**C***), which pairs with A, is incorporated into the growing strand.
2. Before the polymerase moves on, C* shifts back to C; the new nucleotide is now mispaired.
3. The mispaired 3'-OH blocks elongation; polymerase slides back to position the mismatch in the exonuclease active site.
4. The mispaired nucleotide is removed.
5. Polymerase slides forward and resumes polymerization.

uncertainties.description: The heading makes proofreading universal, but page 26 explicitly states that DNA polymerase α has no proofreading 3' -> 5' exonuclease activity. Preserve both. Do not assess the universal "all polymerases" claim.
